subject: Performance benchmarking: methodology differences and next steps

Subject: Questions on MAP benchmarking numbers (TTFT + concurrency)

Ben —

Thanks for the MAP you shared last week. Olivia and I walked through the performance slides and we saw notable differences between the numbers in your document and what our in-house tests are showing. Two quick examples:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) is ~18–22ms on our infra for the same model/config you reported as 35ms.
- At 48 concurrent streams we observe a 2.3× drop in throughput compared to your chart.

We want to progress to close but we need alignment on methodology: what exact toolchain, request fanout, and warmup procedure produced your MAP outputs? It would help if we could reproduce the Redwood run side-by-side.

Can you share a step-by-step repro (including kernel/runtime flags) and any scripts you used? If there are known tooling differences to expect vs our benchmarking rig, please call them out.

Appreciate a concise plan so we can schedule a verification window next week.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme Analytics

Sanjay — thanks for the clear examples. We want to close this fast and avoid any surprises in the final MAP. High-level plan below; details and artifacts attached.

Summary of next steps:
- Share a reproducible bench package (attached): bench script, runbook, and comparison matrix.
- Reproduce Redwood run: we ask Acme to run our script verbatim in a short test window so we can compare traces.
- Live session: optional 60-min screen-share triage if initial repro diverges.
- Contingency: we’ll provide a canary config and a fallback model variant if changes impact latency.

Notes on likely differences we see commonly:
- Warmup: our reported TTFT includes a 5-request scripted warmup to populate KV cache; if that’s skipped TTFT can be higher or noisier.
- Batching: we normalize for continuous-batching at steady-state; single-shot microbenchmarks look better for TTFT but don’t reflect production throughput.
- Tooling: we run a custom kernel selection pass on the runtime; you may see small shifts depending on your container image and CUDA/cuDNN driver versions.

Attachments: acme-repro-instructions.md, redwood-bench-script-v2.sh, comparison-matrix.xlsx

I’ll loop Karthik to provide exact repro commands and a short checklist for the verification window. When are you available next week for the run?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Questions on MAP benchmarking numbers (TTFT + concurrency)

Hi all — quick technical note and concrete repro steps that should remove ambiguity. I attached the exact script we used; below are the critical pieces and the flags that tend to cause divergence.

Critical env/runtime items to match:
- CUDA driver: 525.60 (our infra) — newer/older versions change kernel selection heuristics.
- Container base image: ubuntu:22.04 + intel-mkl disabled for these runs.
- Model variant: quantized-int8-v2 (we reported results for this variant unless otherwise noted).
- Warmup: run 5 sequential generation requests before measuring. This populates KV cache and stabilizes latency.

Repro commands (run from bench/ directory):
- chmod +x redwood-bench-script-v2.sh
- ./redwood-bench-script-v2.sh --model qint8-v2 --seq 1024 --parallel 48 --ttft --concurrency-schedule "ramp:0-48:5m" --driver-check

What the script does (short):
- spawns worker processes equal to requested concurrency and pins each to a logical GPU partition where available
- applies continuous-batching heuristic for variable-length sequences (this affects steady throughput numbers)
- collects per-token histograms and TTFT traces (first token server-side timestamp vs request arrival)

Common failure modes we see when reproductions diverge:
1) Skipped warmup: TTFT baseline shifts and percentiles widen.
2) Different driver/kernel: throughput and TTFT can change 5–15%.
3) Network serialization: if you measure over NAT/proxied paths you inflate TTFT.

If you run the script, please attach the raw JSON trace output (bench/output/*.json) and the driver-check output. We’ll review and produce a side-by-side trace diff.

Happy to join the session — I can do Wednesday morning PST.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on MAP benchmarking numbers (TTFT + concurrency)

Thanks — we kicked off the scripted run this morning and attached the raw output (see Drive link). Early observations:

- With Redwood script verbatim we get TTFT medians that track your numbers closely after the warmup (median ~34ms). Good to see alignment there.
- The throughput drop at 48 parallel streams largely correlates with our GPU topology (oversubscription on a 4x-virtual-GPU node). When we rebind workers to physical GPU boundaries throughput improves by ~1.6×.

We still have two asks before final MAP sign-off:
1) Can Redwood produce a short note on how the continuous-batching heuristic interacts with mixed sequence lengths? We want to show deterministic expectations to our infra team.
2) For competitive comparisons in the MAP appendix, can you include the driver and kernel versions used for each vendor run? That will make the audit defensible.

Proposed Wednesday 9:30am PST for a 60-min triage. Does that work?

—Olivia
Olivia Reed
